findings.mitigation: Apply the R2-stated one-line fix: change lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:48-49 from `return 0` to `scp_policy_check_emit_error "SCP-E001" "" "${label} binary path or expected SHA256 is not configured; set SCP_POLICY_CHECK_${label}_BIN and SCP_POLICY_CHECK_${label}_SHA256 before sourcing this library"; return 1`. If silent skip on unset is intentional for callers that manage binary resolution themselves, add an explicit documented opt-out variable (e.g. SCP_POLICY_CHECK_SKIP_RUNTIME_VERIFY=1) that must be set deliberately rather than silently passing on empty config.

findings.claim: mkdir + chmod two-step pattern persists at all three cache-dir creation sites. Between mkdir -p and chmod 0700 the directory is accessible with caller umask permissions (typically 0755), creating a brief window for same-UID observer processes.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:227-228 (OPA cache_dir), 273-274 (Conftest cache_dir), 367-368 (CACHE_ROOT): all three sites still `mkdir -p "$dir"` then `chmod 0700 "$dir"`. No conversion to atomic `mkdir -p -m 0700`.
findings.impact: Sub-millisecond window where a same-UID concurrent process can enter the directory and observe or hard-link the binary being installed. Residual defence-in-depth gap.
findings.mitigation: Replace all three occurrences of two-step mkdir+chmod with `mkdir -p -m 0700 "$dir"`.

findings.claim: install -m 0755 places trusted binaries world-executable inside the 0700 cache directory. Binary permission bits inconsistent with stated least-privilege posture.
findings.impact: If cache directory ACL is bypassed (CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, admin container, future permission change), binaries are world-executable. Low current impact but inconsistent with the R1-SBP-MIN-04 mitigation that was stated as implemented.

findings.claim: Conftest archive_sha256 verification is silently optional. Future lockfile update omitting archive_sha256 degrades to binary-only verification with no warning.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:264: `expected_archive_sha="$(json_lock_field conftest "$platform_key" archive_sha256 2>/dev/null || true)"`. The `|| true` silences the missing-key exit. Line 287: `if [ -n "$expected_archive_sha" ] && ! verify_file_sha` — skipped when empty. All four platform entries in scp-policy-check.lock currently have archive_sha256, so no active gap.
findings.impact: A 020F Renovate bump PR populating sha256 but omitting archive_sha256 silently loses archive-level verification. MITM or supply-chain compromise of the tarball at GitHub releases would not be caught at the archive stage.
findings.mitigation: Remove `2>/dev/null || true`; treat missing archive_sha256 as lockfile schema error (exit 1 with SCP-E001). If a future single-binary asset genuinely has no archive, add an explicit `archive_sha256: none` sentinel.

findings.claim: SCP_FIXTURE_PATH consumed in CI-parity git diff path without control-character or traversal validation in the local script. CI workflow has Python + bash guards; local script does not.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:328: `git diff --name-only "${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}" -- "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH:-.}"` — no validation. policy-check.yml:249-258 Python guard (rejects empty, \n, \r, \x00) and line 260 bash existence check absent in local script.
findings.impact: SCP_FIXTURE_PATH containing \n injects spurious entries into the changed-files manifest, silently corrupting conftest input. Requires --allow-env-overrides for CI-parity mode to be reached.
findings.mitigation: Mirror policy-check.yml:249-258 in prepare_changed_files: reject control chars, assert non-default path exists under REPO_ROOT.

findings.claim: Local script performs no Sigstore gh attestation verify on downloaded OPA binary. CI workflow (policy-check.yml:207) does. Local-repro and CI paths diverge on supply-chain assurance level.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:207: `gh attestation verify "${BIN_DIR}/opa" --repo open-policy-agent/opa`. scp-policy-check download_opa(): no gh attestation verify call. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Developer operating solely on local runs is at lower supply-chain assurance than CI. A compromised OPA whose SHA256 was committed to the lockfile via a malicious PR passes local verification but is caught by CI Sigstore check.
findings.mitigation: Add gh attestation verify to download_opa() after install, guarded by `command -v gh` with a documented skip-with-warning path for offline environments.

findings.claim: SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH is accepted from the environment in scp-policy-check without being listed in check_sensitive_overrides, enabling a local policy-gate bypass. Setting it to an empty or zero-line file causes zero conftest targets, producing no findings and a pass exit with no warning.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:21: `CHANGED_FILES_PATH="${SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH:-}"`. prepare_changed_files():314-318: `if [ -n "${CHANGED_FILES_PATH}" ] && [ -f "${CHANGED_FILES_PATH}" ]; then return; fi` — accepts any existing file without validation or location restriction. check_sensitive_overrides():73-98 enumerates SCP_POLICY_CHECK_LOCKFILE, SCP_POLICY_CHECK_OPA_BASE_URL, SCP_POLICY_CHECK_CONFTEST_BASE_URL but NOT SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH. lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:145-147: `if [ "${#targets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then return 0; fi` — zero targets returns 0 with no diagnostic. CI path is unaffected (workflow generates changed-files.txt independently in the collect-changed-files step and SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH is not set in the workflow env block).
findings.impact: An operator running `SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH=/dev/null scripts/scp-policy-check` or `SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH=/dev/null python -m standards_control_plane.policy_check` bypasses the local policy check entirely: zero targets, no conftest invocation, exit 0. Additionally, if the file contains entries beginning with `--`, conftest may interpret them as flags (e.g. `--policy /attacker/bundle`) because no `--` separator is present in the conftest_args construction at lib:157. Local-only risk; CI enforcement gate is unaffected.
findings.mitigation: Add SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH to the check_sensitive_overrides guard so that a pre-existing caller-supplied file path requires --allow-env-overrides and emits a warning. In prepare_changed_files, when using a caller-supplied CHANGED_FILES_PATH, validate that each line read does not begin with `-` before appending to the targets array to prevent flag injection into the conftest invocation.

findings.claim: Cleanup trap prefix-match fragile on macOS (TMPDIR=/var/folders/...). Boolean flag replacement not applied.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:101-103: `[ "${CHANGED_FILES_PATH#${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scp-policy-check.}" != "${CHANGED_FILES_PATH}" ]` — unchanged. Line 319 mktemp uses same TMPDIR expansion. Mismatch when TMPDIR unset between mktemp and cleanup on macOS.
findings.impact: Changed-files temp file (repo-relative paths, no credentials) leaked when TMPDIR is unset mid-run on macOS.
findings.mitigation: Replace prefix-match with boolean flag `_SCP_CREATED_CHANGED_FILES` set to 1 at mktemp call, checked unconditionally in cleanup.

findings.claim: conftest_json temp file at lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:156 has no RETURN trap. Python heredoc failure at lines 173-224 leaks the file under set -euo pipefail.
findings.evidence: lib:156: `conftest_json="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scp-conftest.XXXXXX.json")"`; cleanup at line 168 (conftest failure) and line 226 (success only). No trap RETURN guard added in fr2.
findings.impact: Persistent scratch file containing conftest raw JSON output (policy findings, file paths). Non-credential; ephemeral runners reclaim on exit. Low impact.
findings.mitigation: Add `trap 'rm -f "$conftest_json"' RETURN` immediately after the mktemp call at lib:156.

findings.claim: scripts/.tool-versions version pins (opa 1.15.2, conftest 0.68.2) receive no automated bump coverage until 020F Renovate regex-manager ships. Accepted deferral.
findings.evidence: .github/dependabot.yml: github-actions only. No Renovate configuration present. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: CVE in pinned OPA or Conftest version requires manual detection. Interim risk accepted per dispatch terms.
findings.mitigation: No code change at 020B.2. Confirm 020F Renovate rule targets scripts/.tool-versions AND scripts/scp-policy-check.lock sha256/archive_sha256 fields atomically.

fixpoint_assessment.blocker: R3-SAF-MAJ-01 (= R2-SAF-MAJ-01 unclosed): lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:48-49 `return 0` must be changed to emit SCP-E001 and `return 1` before fixpoint can be declared. The fr2 commit message overclaims; the one-line fix specified by R2 was not applied. After that single change, R3 re-review is expected to produce APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (five MIN + three nit carry-forward, one new MIN-06) given none of the remaining findings have an active exploit path in the current CI enforcement route.

r2_closure_verification.evidence: lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:48-49 read verbatim: `if [ -z "$path" ] || [ -z "$expected" ]; then\n    return 0\n  fi`. The R2 mitigation required changing `return 0` to `scp_policy_check_emit_error SCP-E001 ... ; return 1`. That change was not applied. The fr2 commit message ('close 1 R2 MAJ (empty-string SHA bypass blocked)') is inaccurate — the bypass gate is unchanged. In the current main-script invocation path the bypass is not reachable (scp-policy-check overwrites SCP_POLICY_CHECK_OPA_SHA256 from the lockfile at line 383-385, and an empty lockfile SHA causes download/cache verification to fail at verify_file_sha because actual != ""), but for any external caller who sources lib/policy_check_invocation.sh without first exporting the four BIN/SHA256 env vars the silent-pass gate is still live.

scp-policy-check:227-228 (OPA cache_dir): `mkdir -p "$cache_dir"` then `chmod 0700 "$cache_dir"` — two-step unchanged. Lines 273-274 (Conftest cache_dir): same pattern. Lines 367-368 (CACHE_ROOT): same pattern. None converted to atomic `mkdir -p -m 0700`.

scp-policy-check:264: `expected_archive_sha="$(json_lock_field conftest "$platform_key" archive_sha256 2>/dev/null || true)"`. The `2>/dev/null || true` pattern is unchanged; absence of archive_sha256 in a future lockfile still silently skips archive verification.

scp-policy-check:328: `git diff --name-only "${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}" -- "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH:-.}" > "${CHANGED_FILES_PATH}"` — SCP_FIXTURE_PATH is consumed without any control-character or traversal validation. policy-check.yml:249-258 Python + bash guards absent in local script.
scp-policy-check download_opa(): no `gh attestation verify` call. policy-check.yml:207 still has attestation verify in CI. Divergence unchanged from R2.
scp-policy-check:101-103: cleanup guard still uses `${CHANGED_FILES_PATH#${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scp-policy-check.}` prefix-match. Boolean flag replacement not applied.

lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:156: `conftest_json="$(mktemp ...)"` with no RETURN trap. Cleanup at line 168 (conftest failure path) and line 226 (success path) only; Python exit at lines 173-224 still leaks the temp file.
scripts/.tool-versions: opa 1.15.2, conftest 0.68.2 — no Renovate regex-manager present. Accepted deferral to 020F unchanged.
